title: Set a word in wood type in a chase so that it prints the right way round
instruction: Set the word KELP in the chase so that it prints correctly, with the top of every letter toward the far side.
context: Letterpress prints from raised type whose faces are cut mirror-reversed, and the paper meets the forme face to face, so a compositor reads type backwards and sets a line that reads correctly only in the print. Set in reading order as seen from above, the word prints backwards. Done by letterpress compositors and printers (O*NET 51-5111.00, apprenticeship title Compositor; 51-5112.00) in print shops, poster shops and book arts studios. Stamps, relief blocks, seals and embossing dies are made the same way, as the mirror of what they produce.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are centres in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Imposing surface: a fixed steel plate, 20 cm (x) by 34 cm (y), 6 mm thick, centred (36, 0); its top is the bed. Chase: a fixed cast-iron frame on the bed, inside 13 cm (x) by 26.55 cm (y), bars 1.5 cm wide and 1.6 cm tall (below type-high). Furniture: three fixed hardwood strips, 2 picas (8.5 mm) wide, 13 cm long and 1.6 cm tall, running front to back inside the chase, dividing it into four bays, each 6.0 cm wide and 13 cm long inside. Bays 1 to 4 run left to right as seen from the arms, centred at y +10.275, +3.425, -3.425 and -10.275, all at x 36. Bench mat: fixed dark grey rubber, 12 x 60 cm, 3 mm thick, centred (19.5, -3). Wood type: five loose 18-line sorts of end-grain hard maple, each 76.2 mm head to foot and 23.3 mm high (type-high), with set widths and masses K 47 mm, 60 g; E 36 mm, 46 g; L 36 mm, 46 g; P 46 mm, 59 g; J 28 mm, 36 g. Each face carries its capital cut mirror-reversed, as type is (Oswald Bold, 69 mm cap height), in dried black ink on bare maple. All lie face up on the mat with their long side along x: L at (20, +24), P at (20, +16.5), J at (20, 0) and K at (20, -16.5), each with the head of its letter toward the far side; E at (21.5, -25), turned with its head toward the arms. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read from the sorts' poses every control step; in a real trial, a top photo, a mirror and a ruler. The correct forme is the mirror image of KELP: bay 1 P, bay 2 L, bay 3 E, bay 4 K, each with the top of its letter toward the far side (from above the faces read reversed; held to a mirror, the photo reads KELP). A bay passes when all six hold: (1) its required sort's centre, seen from above, lies inside the bay's 6.0 x 13 cm outline; (2) that sort is seated face up: its bottom within 2 mm of the bed (its face 23.3 +/- 2 mm above it) and tilted less than 5 degrees; (3) on the line: its centre within 4 mm, front to back, of the bays' centre line (x 36), so its near end is 26.9 +/- 4 mm from the chase's near inner edge; (4) the top of its letter points within 15 degrees of straight away from the arms; (5) no other sort reaches more than 1 mm into the bay's outline, seen from above; (6) released and still: both grippers' TCPs at least 3 cm from the sort, and it moves slower than 1 cm/s. Score: 1.0 once all four bays have passed together for 1 s (the trial then ends); otherwise, at the end of the trial, 0.25 for each bay that passes. 0, and it stays 0 whatever follows, if any of the five sorts ever falls off the table (its centre more than 5 cm below the table top): dropped type dents or splits. Every other case: a bay earns 0 if it is empty, holds the wrong sort (the spare J included), or its sort is turned head toward the arms, on its side, face down, tilted, off the line, under or beside another sort, or still held. Where the spare J ends up off the chase does not matter. Doing nothing scores 0; KELP in reading order from above (K, E, L, P) scores 0; the right order with E left turned scores 0.75; the right order with the J in place of the L scores 0.75.
reset_notes: Lay the five sorts back on the mat face up as listed, E turned head toward the arms. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Each sort is a box collider; its raised letter and routed shoulders are drawn in the face texture, not modelled. Real lockup closes the forme with furniture and quoins; here the furniture between letters is fixed, the bays' head and foot ends stay open for the fingers, and a 4 mm line tolerance stands in for a galley rail. No ink, paper or press. Sort friction 0.6 (0.5 sliding).
